title: UPDATE: AI Bug Reports Bury Security Tool After Anthropic Debut
summary:
A critical internet security tool is being overwhelmed by a flood of vulnerability notices generated by artificial intelligence, according to Axios. These reports are burying legitimate security alerts and creating excessive noise for the maintainers of open source software, hindering the remediation process.

The surge follows the rollout of Anthropic's OSS Scanner, which uses its most powerful models to perform free vulnerability scans for open source projects. In its first week, the tool accepted 114 of 650 applicants and identified 77 critical and 803 high-severity findings, including a use-after-free memory bug in curl (CVE-2026-92392). Anthropic noted that some of its automated vulnerability reports were subsequently flagged as malware by security systems.

11 days ago, our team @AnthropicAI launched OSS Scanner to give open source projects free, periodic vulnerability scans from our strongest models, inspired by OSS-Fuzz. Some numbers so far:
• ~650 projects applied
• 114 accepted
• 77 critical and 803 high model-rated findings reported (we haven’t scanned all projects yet)

How our reports ended up flagged as malware, and other learnings/updates below 🧵

selectedTweets.bestBit: The first scans have already reported 77 critical and 803 high model-rated findings to maintainers
selectedTweets.quotedTweetText:
A fix I'm excited about: curl, used by countless apps/devices to move data over the internet, just patched CVE-2026-92392. It's a high-severity memory-safety bug (a use-after-free) found with an early version of OSS Scanner.

@bagder called it one of curl's worst vulns in a long time, even if a crash is the likeliest outcome.

Thanks to Daniel and the curl team for fixing and writing it up so openly.
